item.title: Vitamin B12 may hold key to treating a rare genetic disorder: Study

item.content:encoded:
Vitamin B12 may hold key to treating a rare genetic disorder: Study  Scientists discovered that vitamin B12 largely reversed developmental abnormalities in worms carrying a genetic mutation linked to Verheij syndrome, a rare disorder that causes growth problems and developmental delays, as per a study published in the ScienceDaily website.  ANI | Updated: 16-11-2026 23:22 IST | Created: 16-11-2026 23:22 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Scientists discovered that vitamin B12 largely reversed developmental abnormalities in worms carrying a genetic mutation linked to Verheij syndrome, a rare disorder that causes growth problems and developmental delays, as per a study published on the ScienceDaily website. Similar metabolic changes were identified in human patients, raising the possibility that this common vitamin could inspire new treatments for rare genetic diseases. A surprising discovery involving vitamin B12 could open new possibilities for understanding and potentially treating rare genetic disorders. Researchers found that the vitamin can correct developmental problems in tiny worms carrying a genetic mutation associated with Verheij syndrome, a rare human condition that causes developmental delays, impaired growth, and short stature. According to the website, the findings center on a cellular process called RNA splicing, which helps prepare the genetic instructions cells use to produce proteins. During splicing, unnecessary portions of messenger RNA are removed, and the remaining sections are joined together in the correct order. When this process goes wrong, it can disrupt essential cellular functions and contribute to serious developmental disorders. Mutations in genes responsible for splicing can cause conditions such as Verheij syndrome. To better understand the effects of these genetic changes, scientists investigated how a related mutation affects growth and metabolism in a laboratory model. Vitamin B12 Reverses Developmental Defects in Worms The discovery emerged from experiments involving C. elegans, a tiny roundworm commonly used in biological research. The researchers were initially searching for previously unknown genes that influence lifespan when they began examining a mutation in a gene involved in RNA splicing. The same gene is associated with Verheij syndrome in humans. Worms carrying the mutation developed problems resembling important features of the human disorder. Their growth slowed considerably, and they remained smaller than normal. To investigate why this happened, the scientists conducted genetic screens and analyzed the worms' metabolism. They discovered that the mutation disrupted specific metabolic pathways that depend on vitamin B12 and are essential for healthy growth and normal cellular activity. The researchers then tested whether providing additional vitamin B12 could counteract these changes. Remarkably, the treatment restored the affected metabolic processes to normal and corrected the developmental abnormalities associated with the mutation, as per the website. "We were surprised to find that a change in a fundamental process of RNA processing had such a targeted effect on vitamin B12-dependent metabolism," says Jonathan Kölschbach, first author of the study. "Even more exciting was that we were able to largely correct the consequences of this change in the worm model using vitamin B12," added Jonathan Kölschbach, as quoted by the website. Could Vitamin B12 Help Treat a Rare Genetic Disorder? To explore whether their findings might also apply to people, the researchers examined publicly available datasets from human cells. They also worked with Hormos Dafsari, a neuropediatrician at the University Hospital Cologne, to collect blood samples from patients diagnosed with Verheij syndrome. These investigations uncovered evidence of similar metabolic changes in humans, suggesting that the vitamin B12-related pathways affected in the worms may also play a role in the human disorder. Although the results are promising, researchers have not yet established whether vitamin B12 supplementation can improve symptoms in people with Verheij syndrome. Additional studies will be necessary to determine whether the benefits observed in worms can be translated into a treatment for patients. The discovery also raises a broader possibility. Metabolic disruptions may contribute more substantially to diseases caused by faulty RNA splicing than scientists previously recognised. Understanding these connections could help researchers identify new therapeutic strategies, potentially extending beyond Verheij syndrome to other rare genetic conditions. (ANI)

item.description: Bangladesh’s new eligibility status creates an important opportunity for DFC to help address the country’s substantial economic development needs by mobilising private investment, the statement said.
item.content:encoded:
Bangladesh becomes Development Finance Corporation-eligible country Bangladesh’s new eligibility status creates an important opportunity for DFC to help address the country’s substantial economic development needs by mobilising private investment, the statement said. ANI | Updated: 16-11-2026 23:05 IST | Created: 16-11-2026 23:05 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) today announced that projects in Bangladesh are now eligible for DFC financing, the US Embassy in Dhaka said in a statement on Monday. DFC’s investments in South Asia serve as a stabilising force by supporting energy, critical infrastructure, and technology projects that strengthen our alliances and protect the region’s sovereignty, it added. Bangladesh’s new eligibility status creates an important opportunity for DFC to help address the country’s substantial economic development needs by mobilising private investment, the statement said. Expanded access to DFC financing and risk-mitigation tools will help bridge critical investment gaps and advance projects that might otherwise face financing constraints, it said. These investments will spur economic growth by developing critical infrastructure, creating jobs, expanding access to essential services, and strengthening local businesses, it said. DFC’s support is valuable in helping commercially viable, development-focused projects overcome financing constraints or perceived risks that would otherwise deter private investment, the US Embassy said. “Bangladesh’s eligibility for DFC financing marks an important opportunity to deepen our economic partnership and mobilise private investment that delivers lasting growth. By supporting projects that strengthen critical infrastructure, we can unlock economic opportunity for Bangladesh while advancing U.S. strategic interests,” said Ben Black, DFC CEO. “The United States believes that promoting open economies and reciprocal trade will spur economic growth in Bangladesh, and th Agreement on Reciprocal Trade is our public commitment to supporting Bangladesh through this process. DFC financing can play an important role in making that vision a reality – spurring further prosperity in both of our countries,” said Brent T. Christensen, US Ambassador to Bangladesh. Home to more than half the world’s population and some of its fastest-growing economies, the Indo-Pacific offers significant opportunities for strategic US investment. DFC is committed to helping American businesses expand their presence in the region, mobilizing private capital to advance economic growth rooted in free-market principles and strengthening US  economic partnerships, the statement said. The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) is the international investment arm of the United States Government and central to US economic statecraft. DFC mobilises private capital to advance U.S. foreign policyand economic development. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
ASEAN-China Summit: Chinese Premier Li Qiang pledges support for early conclusion of South China Sea code of conduct According to PNA, Lazaro explained that while Beijing and ASEAN member states are pleased with how the discussions have advanced, a “lack of material time” prevented them from finalising the pact before the end of the year. ANI | Updated: 16-11-2026 18:54 IST | Created: 16-11-2026 18:54 IST

Chinese Premier Li Qiang and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr among other leaders at the 29th ASEAN-China Summit (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Chinese Premier Li Qiang has pledged to back the swift finalisation of a “substantive and effective” Code of Conduct (COC) for the South China Sea as Beijing and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) intensify efforts to wrap up talks on the agreement. Philippine Foreign Affairs Secretary Theresa Lazaro announced on Monday. According to the Philippine News Agency (PNA), Li voiced this pledge following his chairmanship of the ASEAN-China Summit held in Pasay City, PNA reported. “An important statement of the Chinese Premier is when he said that he is committed towards an effective, substantive, and early conclusion of the Code of Conduct, which is consistent with the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS),” Lazaro said, as per the state news agency. According to PNA, Lazaro explained that while Beijing and ASEAN member states are pleased with how the discussions have advanced, a “lack of material time” prevented them from finalising the pact before the end of the year. “If we were given another five to six months, we could have finished it. But to say that it will be finished in 2027, (we) give it to Singapore,” she stated, as quoted by the Philippine News Agency. The agency further noted Lazaro's remarks that the Marcos administration has remained “very focused on the COC” and views reaching the 80 percent completion mark as encouraging momentum. “We have done 80 percent or more than that. So, I don't think it's a failure. I think we have done what we have to do as far as Philippines as chair (is concerned). But we didn't have more time,” she said, according to PNA. As detailed in the Philippine News Agency report, the COC is designed strictly to act as a “mechanism for the constructive management of differences at sea,” with participating negotiators concurring that its purpose is not to resolve territorial disputes. PNA also reported that negotiators have already resolved the link between the COC and the 2002 Declaration of Conduct (DOC)—previously one of four remaining sticking points—and have reached a consensus to utilise the completed agreement as a structure for joint maritime cooperation among the parties. Earlier, Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. stated that the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and China maintain a shared resolve to find common ground and advance practical collaboration despite existing regional and global uncertainties. Marcos delivered the remarks during his opening address at the 29th ASEAN-China Summit, which was attended by Chinese Premier Li Qiang. The Philippines currently serves as the rotating chair of the regional bloc. Highlighting the diplomatic milestone, Marcos noted that the current year marks both the 35th anniversary of ASEAN-China dialogue relations and the fifth anniversary of their Comprehensive Strategic Partnership."Even amid regional and global uncertainties, ASEAN and China continue to find common ground and pursue tangible cooperation," he stated, further emphasising that both sides acknowledge the significance of advancing innovative approaches to tackle shared environmental challenges. He stressed that the sides' shared commitment to international law and the peaceful settlement of disputes must be reflected in their actions, including through self-restraint, mutual respect and practical cooperation. Additionally, Marcos pointed out that ASEAN and China continue to actively participate in major trade and investment promotion initiatives to further broaden their economic cooperation. He urged stakeholders to build upon the accomplishments of the partnership to foster peace, stability and prosperity across the region. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
Four members of Baloch family remain missing after reported detentions in Winder and Khuzdar, six others return home Four members of the same family remain missing following alleged detentions by Pakistani forces in Winder and Khuzdar, while six other men who had reportedly been subjected to enforced disappearances in separate incidents across Balochistan have returned home, according to a report by The Balochistan Post (TBP). ANI | Updated: 16-11-2026 18:26 IST | Created: 16-11-2026 18:26 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Four members of the same family remain missing following alleged detentions by Pakistani forces in Winder and Khuzdar, while six other men who had reportedly been subjected to enforced disappearances in separate incidents across Balochistan have returned home, according to a report by The Balochistan Post (TBP). Citing local sources, TBP reported that Frontier Corps (FC) and Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) personnel raided two houses in Winder on October 12. The four family members reportedly remain missing following the alleged detentions. Meanwhile, local sources in Tump, in Kech district, reported overnight raids on several houses by Pakistani forces and members of an armed group they described as a state-backed "death squad". According to the report, those involved allegedly took cash, gold jewellery, vehicles and other valuables from the houses during the raids. The allegations have raised further concerns over the safety of civilians and incidents of intimidation and looting in the region. In a separate development, six men who had reportedly been forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces have returned home, TBP reported. Among those released are three residents of Gujjar in the Mashkay area of Awaran district, who had reportedly been missing since February 2. Their return marks a development for their families, who had been awaiting information about their whereabouts. Meanwhile, the protest camp organised by the Voice for Baloch Missing Persons (VBMP) outside the Quetta Press Club continued for its 6,420th day on Sunday. Visitors to the camp expressed solidarity with families of missing persons and called for an end to enforced disappearances in Balochistan. VBMP Chairman Nasrullah Baloch described enforced disappearances as unconstitutional, unlawful and a serious violation of human rights, demanding the recovery of all missing persons. "If any person is accused of an offence, they should be presented before a magistrate within 24 hours and the legal requirements should be fulfilled," he said. He further held the government responsible for ending enforced disappearances, safeguarding citizens' constitutional and legal rights, and ensuring justice for affected families. (ANI)
